newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin slams United States before summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin slams United States before summit.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin criticised the United States on Monday before this week's summit with Bill Clinton, saying their relations were unequal and Washington had done little to help post-communist Russia.
Yeltsin said in a television interview, the text of which was released by the U.S. network NBC (National Broadcasting Company), that Russia could make no more concessions.
"I don't want a return to the Cold War. I don't want it and our people don't want it, but for that there must be equal conditions in the world order," he said.

Yeltsin is under strong pressure from nationalist and communist foes not to be seen to take a soft line with Clinton over NATO's plans to expand eastwards -- a topic which is expected to dominate the Helsinki summit starting on Thursday.
Yeltsin said that Russia, which has said NATO expansion would threaten its security, was not worried about a possible attack, but about economic and strategic isolation.
"I'm not worried that NATO will attack; Russia would simply hit back," said Yeltsin. "How we can accept a military organisation activating around our borders and openly at that?"
"Why, against Russia's wishes, are they preparing to have (military) excerises in the Crimea, in the Black Sea?" Yeltsin said.
Russia has refused to join excercises, scheduled to be hosted in August by neighbouring Ukraine under the auspices of NATO's Partnership for Peace programme aimed at deepening military ties.
The United States, Britain, Germany and France are among countries due to take part.

Talking tough in the interview on economic issues too, he said: "Why, up to now, can Russia not join various world organisations because of U.S. opposition? Why is Russia not recognised as having a market economy yet? Why? Seventy percent is in the private sector."
"Why are anti-dumping limitations in place against Russia?" Yeltsin asked, referring to trade barriers against cheap Russian goods.
Yeltsin said other countries with much smaller economies had invested more than the United States in Russia since the collapse of communist rule in 1991.
